seoTitle: Cart Abandonment Rate Calculator With Recoverable Revenue
metaDescription: Compute cart abandonment from carts and purchases, the money left in abandoned carts and what an assumed recovery rate could win back.
intro: Computes the share of carts that never turn into purchases and the revenue sitting in them.
why:
Abandonment is a ratio, but it only means something if carts and purchases are counted the same way, for example both sessions or both users. Most carts are never meant to convert, so a high rate alone is not a problem to fix.

The revenue figure shows the size of the pool, and the recovery rate you enter is an assumption, not a benchmark. Use it to judge whether a reminder email or checkout change is worth the effort.
howTo: Enter carts created and completed purchases for the same period.
Set a recovery rate you think is realistic.

faq.q: What is a normal abandonment rate?
faq.a: It varies widely by site and device. Compare with your own history rather than a published average.

faq.q: Why is the recovery rate an input?
faq.a: Because it depends on your emails, audience and offers. The tool does not know it.

faq.q: Should carts be counted by session?
faq.a: Count carts and purchases on the same basis.
